messages:
Lina: FYI starting onboarding of Aureus-14B (community variant). Quick findings from smoke run: vocab entropy profile looks shifted vs our tokenizer, and int4 quant produced a small but consistent embedding cosine drop on our semantic-bench.

Omar: Can you paste the tokenizer stats? token count diff, unknown/tokenization failures? could be NF(K)C or ZWJ stuff. Also which rotary params were exported?

Lina: tokenizer diff snippet: ```
common tokens: 50234 -> 50230 (–4)
max token id: 502999 -> 502999
unmapped: 18 = mostly emojis/zwj sequences
```
rotary: export shows freq_scale=1.0, head_dim=64, head_count=32. No per-head scaling metadata.

Sam: I ran a quick probe on bench-vocab-50k: mean cosine drop ~0.034 after quant int4 (per-tensor), std 0.012. Regression concentrated on tokens that split into two subtokens under our normalizer.

Maya: That smells like tokenmap shadowing + prefix aliasing. If the converter remapped a few high-entropy subtokens to neighboring ids, KV cache indexing + rotary phase could misalign. Check for off-by-one shifts in the token remap table.

Lina: Good call. I diffed the tokenmap and found a small block where multi-codepoint emojis were collapsed to single fallback tokens. Will try remap with `--preserve-subtokens` and rerun.

ci-bot: auto-ci: semantic-embedding-regression on aureus/onboard failed (5/50 examples). Created issue ML-4521 and queued job 1762345800 for a second-run with remapped tokenizer. :warning:

Omar: Plan suggestion: (1) run converter with preserve-subtokens, (2) quant sweep: int8(per-channel) -> int4(per-channel) with ema-calib, (3) a small rotary headwise rescale experiment (multiply rotary angles by 0.995 for head groups 0..7) to see if phase drift reduces embedding delta. If KV alias persists add a tokenmap shim that reassigns the 18 unmapped tokens to dedicated ids.

Sam: I'll run the per-channel int4 sweep overnight and post the embeddings diff. Also will run the biasbench on 100 prompts to ensure no quality regressions beyond embedding delta.

Lina: Thanks. I'll kick off converter + remap now and follow up with logs. Tagging @eng-ml for visibility.

Maya: One more note—if remap fixes embeddings but alters generation probabilities, we should include a small perplexity/LLR check on the eval set before promoting to Dedicated.

Lina: Agreed. Adding LLR and biasbench to the checklist for tomorrow's report.
